subject: maths
source_note: Topic structure follows the IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (AA) guide, the route chosen here for its emphasis on calculus and proof; Applications and Interpretation (AI) is the alternative IB mathematics route. Topic names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

connections.why: Geometric series model compound interest and depreciation
Laws of logs are needed to handle exponential and log functions
Exponent rules underpin geometric sequence formulae
Quadratics are a first family studied with the function concept
Domain and inverse ideas explain rational-function behaviour
Transformations act on the general function concept
Quadratic vertices preview optimisation by calculus
Radian measure defines the circular functions
Identities are used to solve circular-function equations
Circular functions are transformed like any other graph
Derivatives of sin and cos extend differentiation to trig
Bivariate data is summarised before fitting a regression line
Probabilities define the distribution of a random variable
The binomial is a key discrete random variable
Normal calculations are continuous probability calculations
Differentiating e^x and ln x relies on these functions
The derivative gives the gradient for tangents and normals
Setting the derivative to zero locates maxima and minima
Velocity and acceleration are derivatives of displacement
Definite integrals compute areas under curves
Integration recovers displacement from velocity
Integration is the reverse of differentiation
Calculus operates on functions and their graphs
Explorations often model real data with regression
Modelling problems frequently optimise a quantity
